native/resume-token/current.reason: Wire-level boundary placement during resume replay. Production was consistent across the two runs (r1 nmuuicyas, r2 nmuukwo6n): ADD[1], boundary+token, change b, boundary+token, CURRENT[1]+token, boundary+token. fireemu strict sends: ADD[1], boundary+token, change b, CURRENT[1]+token, boundary+token | filters 1:2:0:0:0. Native-gRPC client effect: a raw gRPC listener sees the boundary frames production sends between the replayed changes and CURRENT, and fireemu does not send them. SDK effect not measured: from the Web SDK source a reconnect that stays online raises a remote event at every global boundary, so production may give an intermediate fromCache:true snapshot where fireemu gives the document together with CURRENT; an online-reconnect case in packet L2 is the way to measure it. Issue fs-listen-resume-replay-boundaries. fireemu also sends the count-only existence filter its rule gives every strict resume of a query target without an expected count (the four rows that carry one: older, other-query, without-expected-count, expired/expired); production sent none here. What decides between production's two answers is not recorded.
native/resume-token/current.production: ADD[1], boundary+token, change b, boundary+token, CURRENT[1]+token, boundary+token
native/resume-token/current.fireemu: ADD[1], boundary+token, change b, CURRENT[1]+token, boundary+token | filters 1:2:0:0:0

native/resume-token/older.reason: Existence filter on a resume. Production, identical in both runs (r1 nmuuicyas, r2 nmuukwo6n): ADD[1], boundary+token, change a, change b, CURRENT[1]+token, boundary+token | filters 1:2:0:0:0. Emulator profile sends: ADD[1], boundary+token, change a, change b, CURRENT[1]+token, boundary+token. The emulator profile keeps the official emulator's behaviour here: it sends no ExistenceFilter (firebase-tools 15.28.2, cloud-firestore-emulator-v1.22.0.jar: no class of com/google/cloud/datastore/emulator/impl/firestore or impl/watch references ExistenceFilter or setFilter, and the measured official run sends none), where strict reproduces the recorded production filter. The official emulator resets the target on a resume (RESET, then the full set); the emulator profile sends the exact diff. Native-gRPC client effect: a raw gRPC listener does not receive the filter by which a client checks its held set against the server's count. Issue fs-listen-resume-replay-boundaries.

native/resume-token/older.fireemu: ADD[1], boundary+token, change a, change b, CURRENT[1]+token, boundary+token

native/resume-token/invalid.reason: Production removes a target whose token is not a token (INVALID_ARGUMENT, no ADD). The official emulator (firebase-tools 15.28.2) ignores the token, sends RESET and replays everything; the emulator profile must not refuse what the official emulator completes, so it keeps the RESET. Strict follows production (MATCH).

native/target-protocol/id-after-assigned.reason: Production ends the stream (INVALID_ARGUMENT) when an explicit target id follows a server-assigned one. The official emulator accepts it (ADD[7]); the emulator profile accepts it too. Strict follows production (MATCH).

native/target-protocol/missing-index.reason: Production removes a target whose query needs a composite index (ADD, then REMOVE with FAILED_PRECONDITION). The official emulator ignores index requirements and serves the query; the emulator profile has no index validation, so the target is served and the wait for REMOVE runs out. Strict follows production (MATCH).
